ov: A crocodilian of the rivers of the northern Indian subcontinent, and among the longest of all, with a very long, narrow snout and 110 interlocking teeth built for catching fish. Adult males grow a pot-shaped knob on the snout tip, the "ghara" that gives the animal its name.
wt: Males about 160 kg on average; large males 600–750 kg
rg: Rivers of India and Nepal, with a few in Bangladesh; locally extinct in Bhutan and Myanmar.
df: Mainly fish, swallowed whole; young eat insects, tadpoles and frogs, and adults also take small crustaceans.
fx: It survives in only about 2% of its former range; in 2019 there were at most about 900 in the wild.
The male’s ghara lets it make a hissing sound that can be heard 75 m away.
